newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George warns Clarke on borrowing - paper.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George warns Clarke on borrowing - paper.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George has written to UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke urging that next month's budget should cut the public sector deficit rather than cut taxes, the Daily Telegraph said.
In its Tuesday edition, the Telegraph says the commments form part of a five-page letter from the governor to Clarke ahead of a budget strategy meeting due to be held next Friday.

The paper says George warns Clarke that financial markets could impose an interest rate penalty on Britain if they believe the Chancellor is allowing electoral considerations to allow the deficit to widen.
In the letter, the governor expresses concern that this year's deficit, at four percent of GDP, will be two percentage points higher than forecast in the 1994 budget.
The paper says that George recommends that any money cut from public spending should be used to cut the deficit rather than to finance tax cuts.
